text:
Anna (Support): Hey team — escalation from a customer (high-priority). Their embeddings endpoint is returning normal token rates but vectors/sec is down ~5x and customer sees intermittent `dimension mismatch` errors. Rolling it up here so we can triage. tl;dr: tokens/sec ~3k/s stable, vectors/sec fell from ~600/s to ~120/s, GPU util at 95% and queue depth growing.

Anna (Support): Details pasted from their repro: using `POST /v1/embeddings` model `redwood-embed-1536`, payload of 128 texts per request, batching client-side disabled, we see an error occasionally: `ValueError: dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024` — but most responses succeed, just huge latency spikes.

Anna (Support): Repro curl they provided:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1536","input":["...128 texts..."]}'
```

Anna (Support): They also included a short timeline: problem started ~2026-02-28 14:10 UTC after a config change (they increased client-side concurrency).

Liam (Eng Runtime): Thanks Anna. A couple quick checks: are they using a variant auto-fallback (we have 1536 -> 768 fallback)? dimension mismatch suggests some requests are being routed to a mismatch variant or vectorizer step is inconsistent across shards. Do we have request IDs from the failing calls?

Anna (Support): I asked the customer for request IDs; they sent two: `req_01F...a` (failed) and `req_01F...b` (succeeded). Attaching snippets from their logs: ```
failed: {"req":"req_01F...a","error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024","latency_ms":1432}
success: {"req":"req_01F...b","status":200,"vectors":128,"latency_ms":320}
```

Diana (Infra): On our side I pulled recent service logs for the embed pool around that time. I see frequent batching flushes and spikes in `queue_depth`. Also some worker restarts correlated with OOM-ish mem pressure around 14:12. Sample from controller: ```
[14:11:59] pool=embed-1536 queue_depth=2
[14:12:03] pool=embed-1536 queue_depth=48
[14:12:05] pool=embed-1536 worker=vm-52 restart (oom?)
[14:12:08] pool=embed-1536 queue_depth=120
```

Marcus (Eng SRE): I pulled GPU telemetry for the nodes in that pool: `GPU0 util 98%`, `mem 85%`, persistent kernel-level latencies. Looks like continuous batching + client concurrency triggered massive KV cache churn? Also noticed a few tasks routed to a legacy smaller-embedding shard that returns 1024-dim vectors.

Liam (Eng Runtime): That explains dimension mismatch — some traffic landed on the 1024 variant. Two possibilities: our routing table momentarily had a bad mapping (old variant still advertised) or autoscaler spun up mixed-capacity nodes and routing didn't respect variant affinity. Can we verify the routing table snapshot at 14:10-14:15?

Diana (Infra): Snapshot attached from orchestration logs shows a partial rewrite at 14:11 deploying a capacity change: `update_pool embed-1536 target=+20%`. The rollout job hit a flakiness and briefly re-registered an older `variant-1024` back into the discovery set before removing it. I think requests during that window were mixed.

oncall-bot: ALERT fired: embedding-pool-high-queue (severity=P2) — pool embed-1536 queue_depth > 100 for 3m (14:12 - 14:15).

Liam (Eng Runtime): Ok. Quick mitigations: 1) Pin routing so only 1536 variant serves prod traffic (disable fallback) for that customer's route as temporary mitigation. 2) Reduce `batch_max` and increase `batch_timer_ms` to avoid huge batch pressure that saturates GPU memory. 3) Add a soft rate-limit if client concurrency spikes. Anyone wants to do the canary?

Anna (Support): I proposed the pin to the customer and they asked for a timeline. They agreed to pause high concurrency while we try the canary.

Diana (Infra): I'll apply a canary rollback: remove variant-1024 from discovery for the embed-1536 pool for 5 minutes and monitor. Making change now (canary id cny-3321).

deploy-bot: Started canary cny-3321: remove variant-1024 from pool embed-1536 -> staging -> prod (k=3).

Diana (Infra): Canary applied. Also bumped `batch_timer_ms` from 5 -> 25ms and decreased `batch_max` from 1024 -> 512 on canary nodes, to reduce mem pressure.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Good. I'm also enabling a routing guard that checks model dimension at the front of the pipeline and rejects mismatches with a 4xx so we don't get misrouted silent failures. Adding a temporary config: `reject_on_dim_mismatch=true`.

Anna (Support): Customer ran a quick test after canary and reported: vectors/sec went from ~120/s -> ~520/s, latency stabilized. They still saw a few 4xx rejects but preferred that to silent mismatch errors.

Marcus (Eng SRE): GPU util on canary nodes dropped to ~70% and queue_depth back to single digits. No further worker restarts in the last 10m.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Sounds like root cause: orchestration race during capacity update briefly re-registered a legacy variant which caused mixed routing; combined with client concurrency causing continuous large batches, led to GPU mem pressure and worker thrash. Fix path: 1) tighten discovery rollout so old variants are removed before new nodes accept traffic. 2) add routing invariant checks (dim match) at API edge. 3) tweak default batch_timer for high-concurrency clients to be more conservative.

Diana (Infra): I'll open infra ticket to harden the rollout sequence and add an e2e test to prevent re-registering retired variants during scaling. Ticket INF-2026.

Liam (Eng Runtime): I'll open runtime ticket RUNTIME-1148 to add reject_on_dim_mismatch and a fallback policy toggle per-route, plus tuning suggestions for batch_timer defaults.

Anna (Support): Customer confirmed resolution and asked for a followup note about recommended client-side concurrency limits and suggested config. I provided them a short doc: `recommendation: if client concurrency > 50, set batch_timer_ms=20-50 and client-side batching=enabled`

Anna (Support): For tracking — closing the escalation after infra/runtime tickets created and customer ok. Summary: transient routing of a retired variant + large concurrent batches -> GPU saturation -> queue depth spike and dimension mismatch. Mitigations applied: temporary pinning/rollback, batch timer/mx adjustments, routing guard.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Follow-ups: I'll draft a short runbook bullet for support describing quick checks (routing discovery, `queue_depth`, `nvidia-smi` on nodes, `reject_on_dim_mismatch` toggle) and include commands to roll a canary.

Marcus (Eng SRE): Leaving a note: observed `nvidia-smi` snippet during spike:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-SXM4-40GB      Off  | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off |                  0    |
| 0    98%  340W P0  85C  Mem: 34430MiB / 40960MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Anna (Support): thanks all. Marking thread resolved in support tracker and linking INF-2026 & RUNTIME-1148. :white_check_mark:

Diana (Infra): I'll keep monitoring the pool for 24h and will revert the canary once rollout logic is hardened. If anyone wants the raw logs I pulled I can drop them in the incident S3.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Great work. We'll follow up with PRs and update the customer with the long-term fix ETA. :rocket:
